title: Ideal vs. Non-Ideal Solutions & Azeotropic Mixtures
topics: Ideal Solutions (A-B = A-A = B-B; ΔH_mix = 0, ΔV_mix = 0, ΔS_mix > 0, ΔG_mix < 0; Benzene/Toluene)
Non-Ideal Solutions with Positive Deviations (A-B < A-A/B-B; ΔH_mix > 0, ΔV_mix > 0; Minimum Boiling Azeotrope)
Non-Ideal Solutions with Negative Deviations (A-B > A-A/B-B; ΔH_mix < 0, ΔV_mix < 0; Maximum Boiling Azeotrope)

quickSummary: Ideal: ΔH_mix=0, ΔV_mix=0 (Benzene+Toluene). Positive deviation: A-B weaker, ΔH>0, ΔV>0, forms Minimum Boiling Azeotrope (95.6% Ethanol). Negative deviation: A-B stronger, ΔH<0, ΔV<0, forms Maximum Boiling Azeotrope (68% HNO₃, Acetone+Chloroform).
summary: Master ideal vs non-ideal thermodynamics, molecular interactions, and minimum/maximum boiling azeotropes.

conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Ideal Solutions Thermodynamics

summaryBox.title: Ideal Solutions
summaryBox.takeaway: Obeys Raoult's law at all concentrations. ΔH_mix = 0, ΔV_mix = 0, ΔS_mix > 0, ΔG_mix < 0. Intermolecular forces A-B = A-A = B-B.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
IDEAL SOLUTION THERMODYNAMICS

Δ_mix H = 0  |  Δ_mix V = 0  |  Δ_mix S > 0  |  Δ_mix G < 0

Examples: Benzene + Toluene; n-Hexane + n-Heptane; Bromoethane + Chloroethane; Chlorobenzene + Bromobenzene.
conceptBreakdown.content: An ideal solution obeys Raoult’s Law across the entire concentration range. The cohesive forces between solute-solute ($B-B$) and solvent-solvent ($A-A$) are identical to adhesive solute-solvent ($A-B$) interactions.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Non-Ideal Solutions & Azeotropic Mixtures
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Non-Ideal Solutions & Azeotropic Mixtures
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NON-IDEAL SOLUTIONS & AZEOTROPES

1. POSITIVE DEVIATION:
   • A-B forces WEAKER than A-A and B-B
   • Δ_mix H > 0 (Endothermic) | Δ_mix V > 0 (Expansion) | P_total > Ideal
   • Forms MINIMUM BOILING AZEOTROPE (Boils lower than pure components)
   • Example: Ethanol (95.6%) + Water (4.4%) (Boils at 351.15 K)

2. NEGATIVE DEVIATION:
   • A-B forces STRONGER than A-A and B-B (e.g., H-bonding in Acetone + Chloroform)
   • Δ_mix H < 0 (Exothermic) | Δ_mix V < 0 (Contraction) | P_total < Ideal
   • Forms MAXIMUM BOILING AZEOTROPE (Boils higher than pure components)
   • Example: Nitric Acid (68%) + Water (32%) (Boils at 393.5 K)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Azeotrope**: A binary mixture boiling at a constant temperature with identical liquid and vapor compositions ($x_i = y_i$). Cannot be separated by fractional distillation.
• **Positive Deviation** $\implies$ Minimum boiling azeotrope (*Ethanol/Water*).
• **Negative Deviation** $\implies$ Maximum boiling azeotrope (*$\text{HNO}_3$/Water, Acetone/Chloroform*).

quickRevision: Positive deviation: Minimum boiling azeotrope (95.6% ethanol).
Negative deviation: Maximum boiling azeotrope (68% HNO₃).
Acetone + Chloroform exhibits negative deviation due to H-bonding.
